title: Migration 21 — DDP-controlled farmer provisioning
description:
Applies a pre-21 world stage, then migration 21, and rolls 21 back; baseline is the state immediately before 21. Scores VERIFY sections A, B and C. 21 makes DDP-controlled farmer provisioning real: a brand-new auth user must land as 'pending' rather than 'farmer', so self-signup cannot mint an operational farmer.

This is the only fixture that needs an explicit pre-migration world, and the reason is structural rather than incidental. The substrate models a post-22 database because five fixtures for later migrations need has_operational_farmer_access(), which migration 22 creates. Migration 21's rollback opens with an ordering guard that refuses to run while 22 is applied -- correctly, since 22's policies are written in terms of the provisioning model 21 installs. On a post-22 substrate that guard therefore always fires and 21's reversibility can never be examined. The pre-21 stage runs BEFORE the symmetry baseline is captured, so it is part of the world rather than a correction applied to the result.

Object counts do not move across this fixture (114 -> 114 -> 114) because 21 replaces rather than creates. What makes it non-vacuous is the definition digest: handle_new_user()'s body differs between baseline and applied, so a rollback that failed to restore the prior body would be reported even though every object name and signature matched.
